audio_caption: The audio clip begins with a male speaker introducing a video about autophagy, promising to reveal the truth about how long it takes for it to begin. He encourages the listener to like and subscribe. Next, he announces he will quickly go through some of the basics. The clip ends abruptly with a distinct "click" sound.

The clip begins with a male voice, speaking in a conversational tone, explaining "autophagy is a metabolic process that starts converting cellular debris." The speaker goes on to summarize autophagy as a type of "self-eating," and encourages viewers to check out a video giving an overview of autophagy. The clip ends with a single, short sound effect, specifically a "click".

The audio clip begins with a male speaker, in an informative tone, stating that research shows signaling happens through pathways of "mTOR and AMPK." He continues, explaining that mTOR, or mammalian target of rapamycin, is the body's master nutrient regulator that affects cellular growth, protein synthesis, and anabolism.

A male voice speaks in a somewhat educational tone about AMPK and its function as a fuel sensor, mentioning its role in energy homeostasis and autophagy. Then he explains mTOR's inhibition of autophagy due to its growth-promoting action, contrasting it with AMPK's support for autophagy. The voice continues explaining AMPK's role in inhibiting cellular growth during nutrient deprivation by suppressing the mTORC1 pathway and the consequent catabolization of weak components.

The audio clip features one male speaker in a relatively calm, informative tone discussing autophagy. He notes that the "more depleted your body is of certain nutrient factors... the bigger the reason for triggering autophagy." He explains that both "mTOR and AMPK sense the presence of nutrients" and cells decide whether to be "anabolic or catabolic." This is followed by music, which has a slightly tense, cinematic feel.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker discussing a process determined by growth factors and mentioning insulin, IGF1, and mechanical muscle stimuli. He then describes how insulin and IGF1 signal the presence of anabolic nutrients, promoting storage and growth, and activating a pathway that leads to muscle protein synthesis, contrasting this with autophagy. The clip ends with the speaker stating that this process is the opposite of autophagy.

The audio clip features a single male speaker delivering a monologue in a neutral, informative tone about the effects of carbohydrates and proteins on autophagy. He mentions "raising insulin and blood sugar," being "catabolic," and inhibiting autophagy even with nutrient presence. The speaker then emphasizes how amino acids and protein decrease the necessity for activating autophagy, also explaining that protein restriction isn't an effective way of trying to increase autophagy or lifespan.

A male speaker states that "calories from any macronutrient" will "suppress autophagy," mentioning protein, carbs, ketones, and fats and their effect on "mtor," "insulin," and "AMPK," in a declarative tone. He explains that, although the spike of insulin isn't as high when consuming fat, "it'll still be directed into storage eventually," which, he says, decreases the body's need for autophagy.

The audio clip features a single male speaker explaining how autophagy is regulated in your cells. He lists examples such as "nutrient status", amino acid access, fasting length, blood sugar, insulin, caloric intake, and body's "energetic demand". The speaker uses a clear and informative tone.

The audio clip features a single male speaker discussing autophagy. The speaker explains the need for fasting to activate autophagy and the rationale behind it, discussing glucose-ketone index and insulin-to-glucagon ratio. The speaker has a neutral, informative speaking tone. The end of the audio clip features a short sound.

The clip begins with a male speaker inquiring about when autophagy kicks in. Another male speaker, with a knowledgeable tone, explains that it depends on nutrient status and the presence of nutrients in the bloodstream. He describes that those who consume fewer carbs and protein on a daily basis will more quickly enter autophagy, opposed to those who consume more calories. This is followed by the first speaker asking to have a Milky Way candy bar. The second speaker warns that more carbs and protein mean a longer fast to get into autophagy, and that excess calories increase the buffer zone. The second speaker concludes that mild calorie restriction and staying around maintenance calories is optimal, as this will help the body go into autophagy faster without extensive fasting, which can have negative side effects.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker discussing autophagy. He uses a somewhat excited and informative tone as he lists ways to activate it, such as fasting, calorie restriction, exercise, and resistance training. The speaker clarifies the roles of "mTOR" and autophagy in different body regions. Suddenly, the speech cuts off abruptly and is replaced by a loud, quick buzzer sound that ends the recording.

The clip begins with a male speaker addressing the audience, stating that the video should provide insight into autophagy, but it is not black and white, and will vary between people and their diets. He briefly describes the effects different diets have on initiating autophagy, and then mentions that intermittent fasting is one of the most effective ways of activating pathways. He ends the clip by telling the audience to like and subscribe. The sounds of a foghorn conclude the clip.
